metadata.purpose: Insider K-12 school insights — district nuances, magnet/IB access tricks, AP scheduling realities, principal turnover patterns, transfer paths, things admissions tours don't mention.

sections.title: District mechanics most parents don't know

items.label: Within-district transfer windows are short
items.detail: Most public districts have a fixed transfer-request window in winter (Jan-Feb typically). After that, switching schools mid-year requires hardship documentation. Plan ahead if your kid's assigned school isn't a fit.

items.label: Magnet/option-school lottery odds vary by sibling priority
items.detail: Bellevue's Spanish Immersion at Stevenson and Lake Washington's Mandarin programs both heavily favor sibling preference. First-child-in-family entry can be 5-15% acceptance; sibling backfill rate is 80%+. If you have multiple kids, getting the first one in is the high-leverage move.

items.label: Principal turnover affects program continuity
items.detail: AP/IB programs often shrink or expand based on the principal's priorities. Check the school's most recent 3 years of AP course offerings on the state report card — declining lists are a yellow flag, regardless of the school's overall reputation.

items.label: AP course count != AP access
items.detail: A school with 18 AP courses listed often has only 8-10 actually offered in any given year (insufficient enrollment cancels sections). Ask the counseling office: 'How many AP sections actually ran last year and which?' That's the real number.

items.label: AP weighting depends on school policy, not transcript
items.detail: GPA boost for APs varies by school — some weight all APs equally, others only weight 'core' APs. UC GPA recalculation only weights up to 8 semesters of AP/honors. Ask before assuming a 5.0 boost on every AP.

items.label: IB Diploma programs require sustained 11-12 commitment
items.detail: IB Diploma can't be partial — you commit junior year and finish senior year. Switching out mid-program means losing IB credit but staying for the courses. Worth confirming the school has a robust IB advising track.

items.label: Choice transfer + tuition options exist for non-resident families
items.detail: Most WA districts accept choice transfers from out-of-district families, sometimes with tuition. Bellevue, Lake Washington, and Mercer Island all run modest-tuition non-resident programs that bypass residential requirements. Apply by Feb 1 typically.

items.label: Top private schools' financial aid is more generous than published
items.detail: Lakeside, Bush, and Seattle Academy all publish 'avg aid award' numbers but the reality is often higher for families under $200K household income. Apply even if the sticker shock seems extreme — actual cost can be 30-60% of list.

items.label: Public school open enrollment wave 2 (May-June)
items.detail: Districts often open a second enrollment wave for late-decided families after the main March deadline. Check the district website in mid-May — fewer parents apply, popular programs sometimes have spots.

items.label: STEM magnet entry timing varies by district
items.detail: Tesla STEM HS (Lake Washington) requires application from 8th grade fall — most parents discover it too late. Bellevue's Big Picture (project-based learning) entry is by lottery from any 8th grader in the district.

items.label: Highly Capable / Hi-Cap programs have non-obvious entry ramps
items.detail: Most WA districts assess Hi-Cap eligibility via cognitive testing in 1st-3rd grade. If your kid wasn't tested then, request testing at any grade level — the family request is sufficient. Don't wait for the school to flag the kid.

items.label: Running Start at WA community colleges
items.detail: 11th-12th graders can take community college classes free during the school day, earning HS + college credit simultaneously. State-funded. Application happens in 10th grade spring. Worth knowing for ambitious students who max out HS courses early.

sections.title: Data quality flags — context for school ratings

items.label: US News ranking != actual school quality
items.detail: US News K-12 rankings heavily weight AP participation rate + AP exam pass rate. Schools with lower-income demographics often rank lower despite excellent teaching, simply because fewer students take APs. Use the rank as one signal, not the signal.

items.label: Niche.com ratings include parent reviews
items.detail: Niche reviews skew toward parents motivated to leave a review — usually either very happy or very unhappy. Read the full text, not just the star rating.

items.label: Title I status doesn't mean low quality
items.detail: Title I is a federal funding designation for schools serving lower-income students. Many Title I schools have excellent teaching, smaller class sizes (due to funding), and additional support staff. Don't filter them out reflexively.

sections.title: From the field — fresh insider notes (auto-discovered)

items.label: Bellevue HS — Wolverine Guard 100-hour service award
items.detail: Bellevue HS recognizes graduates with 100+ documented community service hours via the Wolverine Guard (WG) award, distinct from district graduation requirements. Worth aiming for if your student is service-oriented — it's a transcript line item colleges notice (verified 2026-04-26 via BHS counseling pages).

items.label: Bellevue HS — Naviance ends 2025-26 for grades below senior
items.detail: Per BSD, only the Class of 2026 (current seniors) uses Naviance for college planning in 2025-26; grades 6-11 are on SchooLinks. Parents asking about Naviance access for sophomores/juniors will get blocked — the right platform is SchooLinks (verified 2026-04-26).

items.label: Newport HS — 90% AP score-3+ rate across 2,706 exams
items.detail: Newport HS posts an extraordinary 90% pass rate (score 3+) across 2,706 AP exams from 1,151 students tested, with 84% AP participation. This is well above WA state averages and a meaningful signal of AP-instruction quality, not just course availability (verified 2026-04-26 via Newport profile).

items.label: Newport HS — AVID program partnered with UW consultants
items.detail: Newport HS runs AVID specifically for first-generation-to-college students with curriculum support from University of Washington consultants — non-trivial because AVID quality varies wildly by school. Newport's UW partnership is a real differentiator for striver-track families (verified 2026-04-26).

items.label: Tesla STEM — Application window Nov 1 to Dec 1 only
items.detail: Tesla STEM admission applications open Nov 1 and close Dec 1 each year via the LWSD ParentSquare portal; the lottery runs in early January (Jan 9 for 2026-27 cycle), with acceptances due Jan 30. Parents who discover Tesla STEM in spring of 8th grade have already missed the window (verified 2026-04-26).

items.label: Tesla STEM — Waitlist moves slowly (#237 still uncalled)
items.detail: As of the 2026-27 cycle, Tesla STEM's 9th grade waitlist next-up number is 237 and has not yet been called — meaning 9th-grade waitlist almost never moves. Don't bank on a waitlist offer; treat lottery rejection as a final answer and apply elsewhere (verified 2026-04-26 via LWSD lottery info).

items.label: Tesla STEM — Locked 4-year CS pathway sequence
items.detail: Tesla STEM's CS pathway is a fixed 4-year sequence: AP CS Principles (9th) → AP CSA (10th) → Data Structures (11th) → Advanced Projects in Java (12th). Students who haven't done coding by 8th grade can struggle starting cold in 9th. Worth pre-prep if your kid plans the CS path (verified 2026-04-26).

items.label: Roosevelt HS — Universal AP enrollment for 10th and 11/12 ELA
items.detail: Roosevelt HS auto-enrolls ALL 10th graders in AP Human Geography and ALL 11th-or-12th-grade students in AP Lang — not opt-in. Even reluctant test-takers will end up sitting at least 2 AP exams. Plan and budget for those fees (verified 2026-04-26 via RHS academics page).

items.label: Roosevelt HS — Jazz Band 1 has won Essentially Ellington 4x since 1999
items.detail: Roosevelt's Jazz Band 1 (dir. Hannah Mowry) has placed first four times at Lincoln Center's Essentially Ellington High School Jazz competition since 1999, most recently 2019 — among the nation's top high-school jazz programs. Audition spots are competitive; serious jazz students should audition early in 9th (verified 2026-04-26).

items.label: Garfield HS — Highly Capable cohort split across 3 schools since 2019-20
items.detail: Garfield is no longer the single HCC destination — since 2019-20, Seattle Public Schools split HC pathways into north (Lincoln HS), central/southeast (Garfield), and southwest (West Seattle). HC-identified students are only guaranteed Garfield if they live in its boundary; otherwise pathway depends on address (verified 2026-04-26 via Garfield PTSA info).
